note: A kind of reader, not a person. Every name, date and line here is fictional; nobody has been sent this page. The personal part (a reader's name) would travel only in the link's fragment, which the browser never sends.
title: For a journalist
reader: a technology reporter covering AI and security
judges: Is there a story, is it fair, and can I verify it without trusting the authors?
why_you: You check before you believe. Every claim in these chapters points at a public record; if one does not hold, or a failure is told too kindly, you are the reader who will say so.

ask.by_note: an example date: nothing has been sent

gets: your name in the acknowledgements, if you want it there
the first edition when it ships
a reply to every comment, and a page showing what your comments changed

chapters.why: the story at its sharpest: the hold, twenty minutes before the talk
a failure told in full: the brakes the team built and never used

chapters_note: A proposal by developer@, from the reviewers study's themes for this reader (A, D, C); the study also says to offer the record, not only the PDF, so each chapter links to its augmented view.

questions.q: What is the headline, and does the chapter earn it?
Which sentence would you quote? Which would you not believe without checking?
Whose side of the story is missing?
What would you ask the editor if you had five minutes?
Which failure is the story, and is it told without excuse?
What could you not verify from the page and its sources?
Does the chapter judge anyone? Is that fair?
Would a reader outside technology follow it? Where would they stop?

short_note: the one chapter to read when short of time: a proposal by developer@ from synthetic@'s runs, for the editor to keep or change
